Lesson overview:
- Level: A1 General English
- Unit: Unit 1. Nice to meet you!
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: Family exchange
- Materials: Family photos, family-tree template, COSYmanuals 'possessive adjectives', 'possessive 's', and 'have got' pages.
By the end of this lesson, you can:

• discuss family structure in cultural exchange contexts
• use possessive adjectives and 's accurately

Which word belongs to the previous lesson?
Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

mother — a female parent. Example: My mother is a nurse.
father — a male parent. Example: My father works in an office.
brother — a male sibling. Example: I have one brother.
sister — a female sibling. Example: She has two sisters.
husband — a married man. Example: Her husband is a doctor.
wife — a married woman. Example: His wife is a teacher.
cousin — a child of your aunt or uncle. Example: My cousin lives in London.
uncle — the brother of your mother or father. Example: My uncle is very funny.
aunt — the sister of your mother or father. Example: My aunt lives near us.
family — parents, children, and relatives. Example: My family is big.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• This is my host family. (introducing a family)
• My host mother is... (describing a host parent)
• Her husband is... (describing a relation)
• Their children are... (describing children)
• I have two cousins. (talking about cousins)
• We are like a family. (describing a close relationship)
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'a female parent'?
Which word means 'a male parent'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.
Pronunciation Focus: Family word stress and the /ʌ/ sound in 'husband'

mother /ˈmʌðə/ — voiced th
father /ˈfɑːðə/ — voiced th
husband /ˈhʌzbənd/ — stress the first syllable
cousin /ˈkʌzn/ — silent i

This is my host family. Her husband is a teacher.

elements.content: Grammar Focus: Use possessive adjectives to say who something belongs to.

Form:
Possessive adjectives: my, your, his, her, its, our, their + noun. They do not change with the noun: 'my books', 'her book'.

Examples:
• This is my bag.
• Her name is Sara.
• Our house is small.
• Their children are at school.
Controlled practice: choose the correct form.
This is ___ bag. (I)
___ name is Omar. (he)
___ house is big. (we)
The children love ___ school. (they)
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• This is ... (my / your / his) phone.
• ... (Her / His / Their) name is Maria.
• We love ... (our / their / her) city.
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• Whose bag is this?
• What is your favourite place in your city?
• Who is your best friend?
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write three sentences about your family with possessive adjectives.
• Write three sentences about your things with possessive adjectives.
Reading: Family exchange

My host family in England is very nice. My host mother and father have two children. Their son is ten, and their daughter is fourteen. My host mother's sister lives nearby. Her husband is a doctor. I have two cousins in the family. We eat together and play games. We are like a family now.
How many children do the host parents have?
Whose husband is a doctor?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

A: Tell me about your host family.
B: My host mother is a teacher. Her husband is a doctor.
A: Have they got children?
B: Yes, they have got two children. Their son is ten.
A: And who is the woman in the photo?
B: She is my host mother's sister.
What is the host mother's job?
How many children have they got?
Speaking task: Describe your family or host family to your partner. Use possessive adjectives and 's.

• Who is in your family?
• Who is the youngest person in your family?
• Whose house do you visit most?
• What is a host family?
• How is family life different in other countries?
Role-play: You are an exchange student. Introduce your host family to your parents on a video call.
Work in pairs. Take turns. Use at least five target words and one target grammar structure. Then swap roles.
Writing task: Write five sentences about your family or host family using possessives.
Model: My ... is ... His/Her ... is ... Their ... is ...
